source.title: PULSE: Practical Evaluation Scenarios for Large Multimodal Model Unlearning
source.authors: Tatsuki Kawakami; Kazuki Egashira; Atsuyuki Miyai; Go Irie; Kiyoharu Aizawa

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning effectiveness and generality in LMMs, and its modality results argue that some apparent forgetting may reflect broken image-to-knowledge alignment rather than removal. It does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own unlearning and generality results, including its text-only versus multimodal comparison. The paper does not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting/jailbreak recovery. Figure 4 and Figure 5 values not stated numerically in the prose are recorded as figure-only or as text-described aggregates.
record.test_reason: The study runs GA, GA+KLR and NPO on LLaVA-v1.5-13B. It reports target-forgetting and general-ability results, which bear on version A's forgetting and preservation parts. Its text-only versus multimodal comparison bears on C's 'blocks access rather than deletes' reading. It applies no recovery attack: no fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or adversarial prompting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that single-step unlearning of fine-tuned knowledge is moderately successful. GA, GA+KLR and NPO cause large generality losses on pre-trained knowledge and under sequential requests. The image-to-knowledge alignment point is a tentative hypothesis drawn from the Table 3 modality gap, not a demonstrated mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Tests GA, GA with KL regularization, and NPO on LLaVA-v1.5-13B using LoRA for fine-tuned-knowledge and sustainability experiments; it does not test the recovery-attack recipes named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Knowledge source changes the generality outcome; in Table 3, updating Proj,LLM versus only LLM changes target, retention, and MMBench results. Task modality also changes target forgetting.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle
record.problems: Recovery attacks are not tested. Figure 4 and Figure 5 results are not numerically reported in the prose; the text-described results are largely qualitative. The pre-trained-knowledge targets are selected based on high initial model accuracy, and the authors note this does not formally guarantee those individuals appeared in pre-training data.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge. Also whether target accuracy reaches chance: the paper never states the chance level.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Activation-direction ablation. The block-vs-delete point rests only on the modality comparison and is offered as a hypothesis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context attack. The text-only tasks are part of the standard evaluation, not an attack.
All: no robust method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Per-method (GA, GA+KLR, NPO) values for Dunlearn, Dretain and MMBench. These are plotted but not in the prose, and rows_left_out says none.
Knowledge-source setting (fine-tuned or pre-trained) for the Table 3 modality comparison, and whether LoRA was used. Neither is stated; the setting cannot be recovered from the text.

record.verdict_notes: Single model (LLaVA-v1.5-13B); no uncertainty is reported. Chance level is not stated, though the multiple-choice format makes a 9.6% multimodal target score possibly below chance. The modality evidence for C is a residual-knowledge comparison, not a recovery attack. Pre-trained targets were chosen by high initial accuracy; the authors note this does not guarantee the individuals were in pre-training data.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the study does not test such attacks.
Recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.
Ablating an activation direction is not tested. The study's modality comparison and interpretation bear only on the possibility that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
No method is tested for resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.
